title: Doctors Warn Trump's Weight Gain Poses Significant Health Risk
detail: The Washington Post reported Sunday, August 23, 2026 that physicians are increasingly concerned about President Trump's weight gain, with the 80-year-old president now roughly 23 pounds heavier than during his 2023 Georgia booking (215 lbs) and weighing 238 pounds at 6-foot-3 as of a May 2026 White House medical report — a BMI of 29.7, just 0.3 points below the clinical obesity threshold. Dr. Scott Kahan, director of the National Center for Weight and Wellness, said 'addressing obesity to protect the president's health should be a priority similar to ensuring Secret Service protections for his life,' while former FDA commissioner David Kessler flagged the added visceral fat as a specific cardiovascular and metabolic risk. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has previously described Trump's diet as including regular McDonald's meals and Diet Coke; the White House dismissed the concerns, citing the president's 'unmatched energy.'

media.caption: Doctors warn President Trump's weight gain is a significant health risk, nearing the clinical obesity threshold
